newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-NZ FIGHT BACK BUT ENGLAND IN COMMAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ FIGHT BACK BUT ENGLAND IN COMMAND.

text.p: New Zealand fought back on the third day of the second cricket test on Saturday but will have to bat for two days to save the match against England at the Basin Reserve.
New Zealand were 48 without loss at the close, still requiring 211 to make England bat a second time.
Opener Bryan Young was unbeaten on 32 at stumps with Blair Pocock on 13.
England began the day at 204 for three wickets and went on to reach 363. But at five for 331 they had promised a more imposing total.
Left-hander Graham Thorpe hit 108, his fourth test hundred and his second in consecutive innings in this series.
He received good support from Nasser Hussain, who made 64, and John Crawley, whose 56 was part of a 118-run stand for the fifth wicket.
England lost three wickets in the space of 20 balls with the total on 331.
Fast-medium bowler Simon Doull finished with five for 75, his fourth haul of five or more wickets in a test innings.
His last wicket, Darren Gough, was his 50th in his 15th test.
Debutant teenage spinner Daniel Vettori took two for 98 from 34.3 overs, with Geoff Allott, Nathan Astle and Dipak Patel picking up one wicket apiece.
Thorpe fell to a sharp stumping while facing off-spinner Patel on 108. He left his crease momentarily for a drive only to be beaten by Patel's turn and keeper Lee Germon quickly had the bails off.
Thorpe batted for 329 minutes, faced 249 balls and hit 12 boundaries for his fourth test hundred, and together with Crawley added 118 in 180 minutes for the fifth wicket.
Crawley was hit a nasty blow to the head by an Allott bouncer and soon after edged Doull to Germon after making 56.

In the New Zealand second innings, England captain Mike Atherton quickly bought his spinners Robert Croft and Phil Tufnell into action but the batsman faced few problems giving the kiwis some hope of a draw.
The first test of the three-match series was drawn.
